title: From a fault to a next step.
summary: Follow a support question through validation, retrieval, and a guided response.
scenario: “The charger at Example Plaza is not starting. What should I check?”

steps.label: Question
steps.title: Understand the request
steps.body: The fictional operator names a location and a symptom. The assistant first needs enough context to identify the charger and the kind of problem.

steps.label: Validate
steps.title: Resolve the equipment
steps.body: A lookup tool would validate the charger against authorized operational data. In this illustration, Example Plaza is a fictional location; no lookup is performed.

steps.label: Retrieve
steps.title: Find relevant procedures
steps.body: Keyword and semantic retrieval surface relevant troubleshooting material. Reranking helps prioritize passages related to the reported symptom.

steps.label: Reason
steps.title: Choose the response path
steps.body: The available evidence determines whether to explain a known issue, suggest a documented check, or ask the operator a focused follow-up question.

steps.label: Respond
steps.title: Offer a grounded next step
steps.body: The assistant would deliver a clear, contextual next step. Operational actions are handled through validated tools, not through an unsupported claim that an action succeeded.

title: A question becomes an answer.
summary: See how natural-language analytics stays connected to bounded, scoped data access.
scenario: “How did charging energy change at my locations last week?”

steps.label: Question
steps.title: Identify the analytical intent
steps.body: The question asks for a time-based energy comparison. The application supplies the authorized user context and the assistant selects a suitable analytics tool.

steps.label: Scope
steps.title: Apply the authorized scope
steps.body: Access boundaries come from the application session. The model cannot expand the request to another operator's locations.

steps.label: Query
steps.title: Run a prepared query
steps.body: The selected tool uses a predefined, parameterized query. It does not execute model-generated SQL. This walkthrough does not connect to any database.

steps.label: Check
steps.title: Check what came back
steps.body: A typed result makes the available fields and empty-data behavior explicit. Cached or pre-aggregated data can reduce repeated computation.

steps.label: Explain
steps.title: Explain the result in context
steps.body: The final response describes the comparison supported by the returned data. Missing information should be acknowledged rather than filled with invented figures.

title: A location becomes a proposal.
summary: Explore the separation between analysis, deterministic calculations, and proposal writing.
scenario: “Prepare a charging-site proposal for this example location and budget.”

steps.label: Inputs
steps.title: Collect the site assumptions
steps.body: A site location and cost assumptions establish the task. In a real proposal, missing assumptions need to be requested before the analysis proceeds.

steps.label: Analyze
steps.title: Build the site and market context
steps.body: Tools collect the inputs relevant to feasibility. The agent coordinates those tools and organizes the resulting evidence.

steps.label: Calculate
steps.title: Keep financial math deterministic
steps.body: Python tools compute financial projections from explicit inputs. An LLM may explain the numbers, but does not invent the calculations.

steps.label: Compose
steps.title: Assemble a coherent proposal
steps.body: The workflow turns the analysis into a structured document. The later documented system supports an editable proposal presentation.

steps.label: Review
steps.title: Leave room for human judgment
steps.body: A person checks assumptions and the proposed output before using it. This example produces no financial recommendation or downloadable company proposal.

title: Built for a spoken conversation.
summary: Explore why voice support separates orchestration, operational tools, and speech rendering.
scenario: “Can you help me understand why my charging session stopped?”

steps.label: Listen
steps.title: Capture the spoken request
steps.body: A voice orchestrator manages speech input and the conversational turn. This walkthrough uses text only and does not access your microphone.

steps.label: Route
steps.title: Select a bounded tool
steps.body: The orchestrator selects a tool suited to the question. Typed inputs and application-controlled context define the request boundary.

steps.label: Execute
steps.title: Handle the operational work
steps.body: The tool service applies domain logic. Work that may take longer can return a pending state so the caller receives a short acknowledgement.

steps.label: Render
steps.title: Turn facts into speech
steps.body: Templates render critical operational facts into spoken responses. This helps keep balances, tariffs, and other concrete values tied to tool results.

steps.label: Continue
steps.title: Continue or hand off
steps.body: The conversation can ask for clarification or move toward human help. The roughly 1.5-second turn budget is a documented design target, not a measured result shown here.
